title: Anisotropic Structural and Magnetic Response in Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$: Al-Sublattice Reconstruction upon Sm Substitution
abstract: Chemical pressure plays a critical role in determining the crystal structures and physical properties of intermetallic compounds. Here, we report the synthesis, crystal structure, and physical properties of Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$, a structural analog of UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$, in which the smaller 5f uranium atoms are replaced by larger 4f samarium atoms. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a tetragonal $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\times1$ superstructure with space group $P\bar{4}2_1m$, derived from a UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$-like average structure with space group $P4_2/nmc$. Comparison with UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ shows that chemical pressure from U-to-Sm substitution produces a strongly anisotropic structural response rather than a uniform expansion of the Ir-Al framework. While one Ir coordination environment undergoes only modest changes, the other exhibits substantial local rearrangement. The Al sublattice primarily accommodates these structural distortions, with selected Al sites showing positional splitting, anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, and partial occupancies, resulting in an Al-rich composition of approximately Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a direction dependence, including a broad anomaly near 50 K for selected magnetic-field orientations. However, the absence of corresponding anomalies in heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and lattice parameters suggests that this feature is more consistent with an anisotropic magnetic crossover than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition. These results highlight how chemical substitution at the f-element site can induce Al-sublattice reconstruction and modify the magnetic response within a closely related Ir-Al structural framework.
summary: This work reports on the synthesis and characterization of $	ext{Sm}_2	ext{Ir}_8	ext{Al}_{31}$, showing that substituting U with Sm induces significant, anisotropic structural reconstruction, especially in the Al sublattice. Magnetically, the material exhibits a distinct, field-dependent anomaly near 50 K, which the authors argue is a magnetic crossover rather than a conventional phase transition, highlighting the strong coupling between structure and magnetism in these compounds.
main_problem: The study investigates how substituting a U element with a larger Sm element in an intermetallic compound ($	ext{UIr}_4	ext{Al}_{15}$ analog) affects the crystal structure and magnetic properties.
main_result: The substitution induces a strongly anisotropic structural response, causing the Al sublattice to reconstruct, and results in a magnetic anomaly near 50 K interpreted as a crossover rather than a bulk phase transition.
method: The research combines single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD) to determine structure, magnetic susceptibility measurements ($\chi$) to probe magnetism, and heat capacity measurements ($C_p$) to check for thermodynamic transitions.
model_or_system: The physical system is the intermetallic compound $	ext{Sm}_2	ext{Ir}_8	ext{Al}_{31}$, which is structurally analogous to $	ext{UIr}_4	ext{Al}_{15}$. The investigation focuses on the local environment and electronic interactions influenced by the f-element substitution.
key_observables: Crystal structure (tetragonal superstructure $P ar{4}2_1m$), anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) showing a broad anomaly near 50 K, and the absence of corresponding heat capacity anomalies.
important_parameters: The substitution element (U $	o$ Sm), the temperature of the magnetic anomaly ($\sim 50 	ext{ K}$), and the structural distortion magnitude.
main_assumptions: The magnetic anomaly at 50 K is interpreted as an anisotropic magnetic crossover rather than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition due to the lack of corresponding signals in $C_p$ or lattice parameters.
figures_summary: Figures show the crystal structure and PXRD pattern of $	ext{Sm}_2	ext{Ir}_8	ext{Al}_{31}$; supplementary figures detail lattice parameters, temperature dependence, and structural refinement data.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by synthesizing and characterizing the structure of $	ext{Sm}_2	ext{Ir}_8	ext{Al}_{31}$ via SCXRD, comparing its structural response to the parent compound $	ext{UIr}_4	ext{Al}_{15}$. It then analyzes the resulting structural distortions, particularly in the Al sublattice, before presenting magnetic susceptibility data to characterize the magnetic ground state.
why_interesting: The interplay between chemical pressure, structural reconstruction (Al sublattice), and the resulting magnetic anisotropy in f-electron materials is highly relevant to understanding crystal electric field effects and magnetic ordering in correlated systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1| Crystalline structure of Sm2Ir8Al31. (a) Crystal structure of Sm2Ir8Al31. (b) Powder X-ray diffraction pattern of Sm2Ir8Al31 and the corresponding Rietveld refinement. The inset shows single crystals on millimeter-grid paper.

Fig. 2| Crystalline structure of Sm2Ir8Al31. (a) Crystal structures shown using the average cell and the √2 × √2 × 1 supercell. (b) Reciprocal-space intensity of Sm2Ir8Al31 along the xkl, hxl, and hkx directions. (c) Reciprocal-space intensity map illustrating the relationship between the average-cell and supercell reciprocal lattices. The average structure adopts the same structural framework as UIr4Al15, whereas the superstructure exhibits a (√2 × √2 × 1) enlargement of the unit cell.

Fig. 3 | The structure comparison between Sm2Ir8Al31 and UIr4Al15. (a) Comparison of the average structures, highlighting the Al sites with pronounced positional disorder. (b) Local structural distortion around the Sm/U and Ir framework, illustrated by selected interatomic distances and bond angles. (c) Anisotropic displacement and splitting of the Al sublattice in Sm2Ir8Al31.

Fig. 4 | Temperature-dependent properties of Sm2Ir8Al31. (a) magnetic susceptibility measured at 10 kOe for different field orientations under ZFCW and FC conditions; (b) Comparison of the atomic displacement ellipsoids of Sm2Ir8Al31 (top) and UIr4Al15 (bottom), showing different anisotropic atomic displacement patterns; The blue shading highlights the in-plane atomic displacement of the Sm and Ir2 atoms within the ab plane, which show relatively small positional changes upon replacing U with Sm. (c) normalized electrical resistance under different magnetic fields, as shown in the inset; and (d) zero-field heat capacity, with the Debye mode fitting in the inset.
